parts.title: Frozen Food
parts.passageHtml:
{[Frozen Food][1734672]}

{[A US perspective on the development of the frozen food industry][1734676]}

{[At some point in history, humans discovered that ice preserved food.][1734688]} {[There is evidence that winter ice was stored to preserve food in the summer as far back as 10,000 years ago.][1734700]} {[Two thousand years ago, the inhabitants of South America’s Andean mountains had a unique means of conserving potatoes for later consumption.][1734722]} {[They froze them overnight, then trampled them to squeeze out the moisture, then dried them in the sun.][1734743]} {[This preserved their nutritional value—if not their aesthetic appeal.][1734762]}

{[Natural ice remained the main form of refrigeration until late in the 19th century.][1734774]} {[In the early 1800s, ship owners from Boston, USA, had enormous blocks of Arctic ice towed all over the Atlantic for the purpose of food preservation.][1734789]} {[In 1851, railroads first began putting blocks of ice in insulated rail cars to send butter from Ogdensburg, New York, to Boston.][1734816]}

{[Finally, in 1870, Australian inventors found a way to make ’mechanical ice’.][1734839]} {[They used a compressor to force a gas - ammonia at first and later Freon—through a condenser.][1734851]} {[The compressed gas gave up some of its heat as it moved through the condenser.][1734866]} {[Then the gas was released quickly into a low-pressure evaporator coil where it became liquid and cold.][1734882]} {[Air was blown over the evaporator coil and then this cooled air passed into an insulated compartment, lowering its temperature to freezing point.][1734899]}

{[Initially, this process was invented to keep Australian beer cool even in hot weather.][1734924]} {[But Australian cattlemen were quick to realize that, if they could put this new invention on a ship, they could export meat across the oceans.][1734939]} {[In 1880, a shipment of Australian beef and mutton was sent, frozen, to England.][1734964]} {[While the food frozen this way was still palatable, there was some deterioration.][1734978]} {[During the freezing process, crystals formed within the cells of the food, and when the ice expanded and the cells burst, this spoilt the flavor and texture of the food.][1734991]}

{[The modern frozen food industry began with the indigenous Inuit people of Canada.][1735020]} {[In 1912, a biology student in Massachusetts, USA, named Clarence Birdseye, ran out of money and went to Labrador in Canada to trap and trade furs.][1735034]} {[While he was there, he became fascinated with how the Inuit would quickly freeze fish in the Arctic air.][1735060]} {[The fish looked and tasted fresh even months later.][1735080]}

{[Birdseye returned to the USA in 1917 and began developing mechanical freezers capable of quick-freezing food.][1735091]} {[Birdseye methodically kept inventing better freezers and gradually built a business selling frozen fish from Gloucester, Massachusetts.][1735108]} {[In 1929, his business was sold and became General Foods, but he stayed with the company as director of research, and his division continued to innovate.][1735125]}

{[Birdseye was responsible for several key innovations that made the frozen food industry possible.][1735153]} {[He developed quick-freezing techniques that reduced the damage that crystals caused, as well as the technique of freezing the product in the package it was to be sold in.][1735168]} {[He also introduced the use of cellophane, the first transparent material for food packaging, which allowed consumers to see the quality of the product.][1735197]} {[Birdseye products also came in convenient size packages that could be prepared with a minimum of effort.][1735222]}

{[But there were still obstacles.][1735240]} {[In the 1930s, few grocery stores could afford to buy freezers for a market that wasn’t established yet.][1735246]} {[So, Birdseye leased inexpensive freezer cases to them.][1735264]} {[He also leased insulated railroad cars so that he could ship his products nationwide.][1735273]} {[However, few consumers had freezers large enough or efficient enough to take advantage of the products.][1735288]}

{[Sales increased in the early 1940s, when World War II gave a boost to the frozen food industry because tin was being used for munitions.][1735305]} {[Canned foods were rationed to save tin for the war effort, while frozen foods were abundant and cheap.][1735330]} {[Finally, by the 1950s, refrigerator technology had developed far enough to make these appliances affordable for the average family.][1735349]} {[By 1953, 33 million US families owned a refrigerator, and manufacturers were gradually increasing the size of the freezer compartments in them.][1735369]}

{[1950s families were also looking for convenience at mealtimes, so the moment was right for the arrival of the ’TV Dinner’.][1735391]} {[Swanson Foods was a large, nationally recognized producer of canned and frozen poultry.][1735412]} {[In 1954, the company adapted some of Birdseye’s freezing techniques, and with the help of a clever name and a huge advertising budget, it launched the first ’TV Dinner’.][1735425]} {[This consisted of frozen turkey, potatoes and vegetables served in the same segmented aluminum tray that was used by airlines.][1735453]} {[The product was an instant success.][1735474]} {[Within a year, Swanson had sold 13 million TV dinners.][1735481]} {[American consumers couldn’t resist the combination of a trusted brand name, a single-serving package and the convenience of a meal that could be ready after only 25 minutes in a hot oven.][1735490]} {[By 1959, Americans were spending $2.7 billion annually on frozen foods, and half a billion of that was spent on ready-prepared meals such as the TV Dinner.][1735517]}

{[Today, the US frozen food industry has a turnover of over $67 billion annually, with $26.6 billion of that sold to consumers for home consumption.][1735545]} {[The remaining $40 billion in frozen food sales come through restaurants, cafeterias, hospitals and schools, and that represents a third of the total food service sales.][1735570]}

instruction.title: Reading passage 1
instruction.content: You should spend about 20 minutes on questions {start_question} - {end_question} which are based on Reading Passage 1 below.

questionSets.title: Questions 1-7
questionSets.instructionHtml: Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.
questionSets.contentHtml:
The history of frozen food

2,000 years ago, South America

  • People conserved the nutritional value of ______ using a method of freezing then drying.

1851, USA

  • ______ was kept cool by ice during transportation in specially adapted trains.

1880, Australia

  • Two kinds of ______ were the first frozen food shipped to England.

1917 onwards, USA

  • Clarence Birdseye introduced innovations including:

    • quick-freezing methods, so that ______ did not spoil the food.

    • packaging products with ______, so the product was visible.

Early 1940s, USA

  • Frozen food became popular because of a shortage of ______.

1950s, USA

  • A large number of homes now had a ______.

questionSets.title: Questions 8-13
questionSets.instructionHtml:
Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 1?
Write
TRUE if the statement agrees with the information
FALSE if the statement contradicts the information
NOT GIVEN if there is no information on this

questions.text: The ice transportation business made some Boston ship owners very wealthy in the early 1800s.
questions.explanationHtml:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
Kinh doanh vận chuyển băng đã giúp một số chủ tàu ở Boston trở nên rất giàu có vào đầu những năm 1800.

Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:

  • early 1800s ~ từ khóa giữ nguyên

  • Boston ship owners ~ từ khóa giữ nguyên

  • ice transportation business ~ had enormous blocks of Arctic ice towed all over the Atlantic for the purpose of food preservation

Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc đề cập đến việc "vào đầu những năm 1800, các chủ tàu từ Boston, Mỹ, đã cho kéo những khối băng Bắc Cực khổng lồ đi khắp Đại Tây Dương với mục đích bảo quản thực phẩm" (In the early 1800s, ship owners from Boston, USA, had enormous blocks of Arctic ice towed all over the Atlantic for the purpose of food preservation).
=> Tuy nhiên, bài đọc không hề nhắc đến thông tin việc kinh doanh này có giúp họ "trở nên rất giàu có" (very wealthy) hay không.

Bước 4: Đáp án: NOT GIVEN

questions.text: A disadvantage of the freezing process invented in Australia was that it affected the taste of food.
questions.explanationHtml:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:

Một nhược điểm của quy trình đông lạnh được phát minh ở Úc là nó ảnh hưởng đến hương vị của thực phẩm.

Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:

  • A disadvantage ~ there was some deterioration

  • freezing process invented in Australia ~ the food frozen this way

  • affected the taste of food ~ spoilt the flavor and texture of the food

Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ "Trong quá trình đông lạnh, các tinh thể hình thành bên trong các tế bào của thực phẩm, và khi băng nở ra và các tế bào vỡ, điều này làm hỏng hương vị và kết cấu của thực phẩm" (During the freezing process, crystals formed within the cells of the food, and when the ice expanded and the cells burst, this spoilt the flavor and texture of the food).
=> Điều này đồng nghĩa với thông tin trong câu hỏi.

Bước 4: Đáp án: FALSE

questions.text: Clarence Birdseye travelled to Labrador in order to learn how the Inuit people froze fish.
questions.explanationHtml:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:

Clarence Birdseye đã đến Labrador để tìm hiểu cách người Inuit đông lạnh cá.

Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:

  • Clarence Birdseye ~ từ khóa giữ nguyên

  • travelled to Labrador ~ went to Labrador in Canada

  • in order to ~ (mục đích của chuyến đi)

  • learn how the Inuit people froze fish ~ to trap and trade furs

Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ "vào năm 1912, một sinh viên sinh học ở Massachusetts, Mỹ, tên là Clarence Birdseye, hết tiền và đến Labrador ở Canada để bẫy và buôn bán lông thú" (In 1912, a biology student in Massachusetts, USA, named Clarence Birdseye, ran out of money and went to Labrador in Canada to trap and trade furs).
=> Điều này trái ngược với thông tin trong câu hỏi. Mục đích chuyến đi của ông là để buôn bán lông thú, không phải để học cách đông lạnh cá. Việc ông bị cuốn hút bởi cách đông lạnh cá của người Inuit là một khám phá tình cờ trong chuyến đi.

Bước 4: Đáp án: FALSE

questions.text: Swanson Foods invested a great deal of money in the promotion of the TV Dinner.
questions.explanationHtml:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:

Swanson Foods đã đầu tư rất nhiều tiền vào việc quảng bá TV Dinner.

Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:

  • Swanson Foods ~ từ khóa giữ nguyên

  • invested a great deal of money in the promotion ~ with the help of... a huge advertising budget

Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ "...với sự trợ giúp của một cái tên thông minh và một ngân sách quảng cáo khổng lồ, họ đã ra mắt 'TV Dinner' đầu tiên" (with the help of a clever name and a huge advertising budget, it launched the first 'TV Dinner').
=> Điều này đồng nghĩa với thông tin trong câu hỏi. "Ngân sách quảng cáo khổng lồ" (a huge advertising budget) chính là "đầu tư rất nhiều tiền vào việc quảng bá".

Bước 4: Đáp án: TRUE

questions.text: Swanson Foods developed a new style of container for the launch of the TV Dinner.
questions.explanationHtml:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:

Swanson Foods đã phát triển một kiểu hộp đựng mới cho việc ra mắt TV Dinner.

Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:

  • Swanson Foods ~ The product

  • a new style of container ~ the same segmented aluminum tray that was used by airlines

  • for the launch of the TV Dinner ~ This consisted of...

Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ "Sản phẩm này bao gồm gà tây, khoai tây và rau đông lạnh được phục vụ trong cùng một khay nhôm chia ngăn mà các hãng hàng không đã sử dụng" (This consisted of frozen turkey, potatoes and vegetables served in the same segmented aluminum tray that was used by airlines).
=> Điều này trái ngược với thông tin trong câu hỏi. Họ đã sử dụng một loại khay đã có sẵn ("the same... tray that was used by airlines"), chứ không phải phát triển một kiểu mới.

Bước 4: Đáp án: FALSE

questions.text: The US frozen food industry is currently the largest in the world.
questions.explanationHtml:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:

Ngành công nghiệp thực phẩm đông lạnh của Mỹ hiện là lớn nhất thế giới.

Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:

  • The US frozen food industry ~ từ khóa giữ nguyên

  • is currently the largest in the world ~ has a turnover of over $67 billion annually

Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc đề cập đến việc "Ngày nay, ngành công nghiệp thực phẩm đông lạnh của Mỹ có doanh thu hơn 67 tỷ đô la hàng năm" (Today, the US frozen food industry has a turnover of over $67 billion annually).
=> Tuy nhiên, bài đọc không hề nhắc đến thông tin so sánh ngành công nghiệp này của Mỹ với các nước khác trên thế giới để xác định nó có phải là "lớn nhất thế giới" hay không.

Bước 4: Đáp án: NOT GIVEN
